title: Lantern and Uniform
premise: Sable Eriksen, a courier for the collapsing Republic of Vessany, carries sealed diplomatic codes toward the border city of Halven Bridge, where an armistice will decide whether the republic surrenders or is erased from the record entirely. Along the road he falls in with a census taker named Ilsa Brandt and a band of displaced clerks who have begun forging their own archive of the war's atrocities. When Sable learns his codes are meant to buy the victors' silence about a massacre at Kesselmoor, he must choose between delivering them and getting the truth on record first. In the end he delivers both — trading his own anonymity and freedom to smuggle the true ledger into the armistice hall, where it is read aloud before the signatures dry.
about_author: Freya Okafor is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing displaced-persons records in post-conflict regions before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about ordinary people who refuse to let institutions finish their sentences for them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Paper
chapters.summary: Sable Eriksen, POV. A courier who prides himself on being forgettable, Sable accepts his final assignment: sealed codes bound for Halven Bridge. He tells himself history happens to other people. Emotional beat: comfortable self-deception established, with a flicker of unease when his handler's hands shake.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. At a checkpoint, census taker Ilsa Brandt asks not just names and numbers but what he saw on the Kesselmoor road. Her questions are forbidden; her notebook is contraband. She lets him pass — and follows. Emotional beat: the first crack in Sable's invisibility, equal parts threat and invitation.

chapters.title: The Clerks' Republic
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. Ilsa brings Sable to a bombed granary where displaced clerks keep a secret ledger of the war: names, dates, the massacre no one will admit to. Their leader, old Archivist Pell, argues records outlive regimes. Emotional beat: Sable glimpses a found family built on paper instead of blood, and resents how much he wants it.

chapters.title: What the Codes Say
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Forced to shelter during a bombardment, Sable breaks protocol and reads his seals: the codes trade recognition of the new regime for burying the Kesselmoor massacre. His mission is complicity. Emotional beat: vertigo and shame as the man who 'just carries things' realizes he has been carrying bodies all along.

chapters.title: Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Pell, POV. The clerks' convoy flees advancing troops; Pell dies shielding the ledger, passing its keeping to Ilsa and, reluctantly, Sable. Emotional beat: grief that hardens into purpose — the found family loses its father but keeps its covenant.

chapters.title: The Victor's Historian
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. In Halven Bridge, Ilsa identifies Colonel Vasch, the victors' official historian, already drafting the armistice narrative with Kesselmoor struck from it. She attempts blackmail with copied pages and is nearly caught. Emotional beat: dread and defiance; the enemy is revealed as a man with a pen, not an army.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Cornered by his own handlers, Sable offers a devil's trade: he'll deliver the codes intact if the true ledger is entered into the armistice record. They agree — then plan to kill him after delivery. Emotional beat: cold clarity; Sable stops being cargo and becomes a player, knowing the price.

chapters.title: Night of Copies
chapters.summary: Ensemble, alternating Sable and Ilsa. The clerks work through the night duplicating the ledger, hiding copies in bread loaves, coat linings, a coffin. Emotional beat: warmth under pressure — the family forged in the granary becomes a network, each copy a small act of faith in strangers.

chapters.title: Read Aloud Before Signatures
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. At the signing, Sable delivers the codes, then triggers the hidden copies: delegates find the Kesselmoor pages slipped into their briefing folders. He reads the names aloud until guards drag him away. Emotional beat: triumphant sacrifice — the truth enters the record even as Sable forfeits his freedom.

chapters.title: Lantern and Uniform
chapters.summary: Ilsa, POV. Months later, under the new regime, Ilsa tends a lamplit reading room where the ledger survives in fragments, copied by hand. Sable, released in a prisoner exchange, arrives unrecognized — and she hands him a pen. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; power corrupts the state, but the record, kept by chosen family, endures.
